newsitem.title: NORWAY: Morgan Grenfell affair deters Oslo share trade.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Grenfell affair deters Oslo share trade.

text.p: Norwegian share prices rose on Monday but volume was thin because foreign investors stayed away in the wake of the Morgan Grenfell affair, dealers said.
The Oslo Total share index rose 0.7 percent to 834.38 points. Turnover was a thin 432 million crowns, including 112 million crowns in Kvaerner resulting from the expiry of options.
"If you take away Kvaerner, this place was a joke today," one dealer said. "Its been a long time since only 18 million crowns were traded in Norsk Hydro."
The industrial giant was up 0.5 percent at 303 crowns.
"Morgan Grenfell has made foreigners more cautious," he said.

Norwegian software house Sysdeco Group ASA learned last Friday its main shareholder was investment fund group Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), currently embroiled in a financial scandal. Sysdeco was down 2.2 percent at 45 crowns.
Another dealer said uncertainties around U.S. interest rates also subdued business.
